content.title: Where to watch Celtics vs. Hornets NBA game free tonight during NBC and FuboTV dispute
content.text: The Boston Celtics’ effort to lock down the Eastern Conference’s No. 2 seed continues Tuesday night against LaMelo Ball and the Charlotte Hornets. The game is scheduled to start at 8 p.m. ET with TV coverage on NBC and streaming on-demand.NBC is part of the NBC Universal family of networks currently blacked out on FuboTV during ongoing contract negotiations. Available streaming alternatives are listed below.How to watch Celtics vs. Hornets on TV and stream without cable:When:Tuesday, April 7 at 8 p.m. ETWhere:TD Garden, Boston, Mass.TV channel:NBC and PeacockStreaming on: DirecTV (free trial) | SlingTV (low intro rate) | Peacock ($10.99+/mo.)Celtics vs. Hornets: The matchupThe Celtics begin Tuesday play having been eliminated for the top seed in the East, and they hold a 2.5-game buffer over the New York Knicks for the No. 2 spot with four games to play. Boston has won three games in a row and 10 of its past 12 to near playoff form at the right time, most recently winning three of four on the road and defeating the Toronto Raptors at home on Sunday. Jaylen Brown scored a game-high 26 points in that contest while Jayson Tatum went for 23 points, 13 rebounds and seven assists.See also: More NBA coverage on PennLiveThe Hornets are very much in the hunt for a better position in the Eastern Conference playoff race after winning four straight and nine of their past 11 games. Charlotte currently sits in a three-way tie with the Philadelphia 76ers and Orlando Magic for the No. 7 spot in the East, and all three are within a half-game of sixth-place Toronto and within two games of the fifth-place Atlanta Hawks. In terms of scoring differential, the Hornets are fourth-best in the East and sixth-best in the NBA, averaging 5.2 points more than their opponents.Celtics vs. Hornets: Know your live streamsDirecTV (free trial): DirecTV offers a 5-day free trial and a total of $30 off over the first three full months for the Choice Package, which includes 125-plus channels and access to ESPN Unlimited, a $29.99 standalone value featuring all ESPN channels and ESPN+.SlingTV (low intro rate): First full month of streaming runs as low as $29.99 with current offer for 50% off Sling’s Orange & Blue Plan. Day passes are also available for 24 hours ($4.99), as well as three-day ($9.99) and seven-day access ($14.99).Peacock ($10.99+/mo.): Peacock’s library of live sports is growing and features exclusive NFL and college football games, all in addition to NBC Universal movies, television series, and more.©2026 Advance Local Media LLC.
